item.title: Git Gitignore
item.description: gitignore and how to use it
item.content:encoded:
.gitignore
> needed to hide files and folders from the Git version control system. Typically, configuration files (especially those with passwords), temporary files and folders are hidden.

Base:

  • Each line is a separate template.
  • Empty lines are ignored.
  • Lines starting with # are comments.
  • The slash character "/" at the beginning of the line indicates the current folder (where .gitignore is located).
  • The asterisk(*) replaces any number of characters.
  • Two asterisks (**) are used to indicate all subfolders.
  • An exclamation mark(!) at the beginning of a line inverts the pattern (used for exceptions).
  • To escape special characters, use the backslash "". To ignore an entire directory, the rule must end with a slash (/), otherwise the rule is treated as a file name.
  • The gitignore repository from github contains examples of gitignore files for all typical projects.

Example .gitignore file

Ignore foo.txt file.
foo.txt

# Ignore html files
*.html   

# But specifically foo.html should not be ignored
!foo.html   

# Ignore rar files in the project root
# Let's say the file /temp/main.rar will not be ignored because he's not at the root
/*.rar   

# Ignore css files from the bar folder not including subfolders
# Let's say the file /bar/temp/main.css will not be ignored because it's in the temp subfolder
/bar/*.css   

# Ignore js files from the bar folder and subfolders, if any
/bar/**.*.js

How can I exclude a folder from tracking but add a subfolder?

Problem 1

Remove the node_modules folder, but leave 2 subfolders jquery and semantic in it

├── js
│ ├── app.js
│ └── system.js
├── scss
│ ├── system.scss
│ └── theme.scss
└── vendor
    ├── node_modules ← Убрать
    │ ├── load-json-file
    │ ├── lodash
    │ ├── jquery ← Оставить
    │ ├── make-error
    │ ├── semantic ← Оставить
    │ └── yargs
    └── semantic.json

Solution:

/vendor/node_modules/*
!/vendor/node_modules/jquery/
!/vendor/node_modules/semantic/

Problem 2

Remove the node_modules folder, but leave the dist subfolder in its jquery subfolder.

├── js
│ ├── app.js
│ └── system.js
├── scss
│ ├── system.scss
│ └── theme.scss
└── vendor
    ├── node_modules ← Убрать
    │ ├── load-json-file
    │ ├── lodash
    │ ├── jquery
    │ │ └──dist ← Оставить
    │ ├── make-error
    │ ├── semantic
    │ └── yargs
    └── semantic.json

Solution:

/vendor/node_modules/*
/vendor/node_modules/jquery/*
!/vendor/node_modules/jquery/
!/vendor/node_modules/jquery/dist/

item.title: Pen on paper
item.content:encoded:
Save important notes on paper

For long-term preservation of notes on paper, it is best to use ballpoint pens.

Why ballpoint pens are the best for archiving

  • Water resistance: Oil-based ink will not smear when wet.
  • Light fastness: the paste does not fade from sunlight for decades.

Paper durability: Ink will not corrode paper fibers over time.

-Chemical stability: pigments are resistant to oxidation.

Disadvantages of gel and capillary pens

Vulnerable to Moisture: Most gel and capillary inks will wash away instantly from water.

  • Fading: capillary pens (liners) quickly fade in the light.
  • Bleed-through: Ink from capillary pens often bleeds through the paper.

Exception to the rule

If you absolutely don't like ballpoint pens, look for gel or capillary pens labeled "Archival-safe", "Document" or ISO 14145-2 compliant. They contain special pigment ink that is not afraid of water and light.

For a home notepad away from the sun, the best choice would be gel pens with pigment ink or classic ballpoint pens.

In such conditions, the main threat is accidental moisture (for example, spilled tea) and the natural aging of paper.

Best options for home recordings

  • Pigment gel: Ideal choice. Pigment-based inks (as opposed to conventional water-soluble dyes) are firmly etched into the paper. They will not flow from a drop of water and write softer than ballpoint ones.
  • Butter ball: Traditional and safest option. The text will not blur, even if the notepad is completely flooded with water.

What is better to refuse

  • Conventional capillary pens (liners): If the air humidity in the room is high, the ink may begin to blur, and a drop of water may cause the text to disappear completely.
  • Cheap gel pens: Blue and black colors in inexpensive sets are often water-based - they smear easily.

Proven series of archive pens

  • Uni-ball Signo (DX or Broad series): Contains Super Ink pigment ink. Protected from water and time.
  • Pilot G-2: A popular gel, but be warned - it has only average water resistance, although it has a long shelf life.
  • Pentel EnerGel: Writes great and dries quickly, but is afraid of water. Use only in dry environments.
  • Pigment liners (Pigma Micron, Staedtler Pigment Liner): These are capillary pens, but with special archival inks. They won't flow.

For a thin, neat line and light blue color in a home notebook, Japanese gel pens with an ultra-thin point (0.38 mm - 0.5 mm) and pigment ink are best suited. Regular roll-on blue is often too dark or muddy, but gel will give a clean, bright shade.

The best pens for your criteria

Uni-ball Signo DX (UM-151), thickness 0.38 mm

Color: Light Blue or Sky Blue.

Pros: An absolute favorite for archival recordings. Uni Super Ink pigment ink is firmly embedded into the paper, is not afraid of water and does not fade. The line turns out to be jewelry thin and clear.

Pilot Juice / Juice Up, thickness 0.38 mm or 0.4 mm

Color: Light Blue.
Pros: The Juice Up version has a unique synergistic nib that writes incredibly smooth for its thickness. The ink is pigmented, moisture resistant, the colors are very rich and aesthetic.

Zebra Sarasa Clip, thickness 0.4 mm or 0.5 mm

Color: Pale Blue or Light Blue.
Pros: Archival quality pigment gel. Convenient clip-on clip. It writes softly, the line is not interrupted, and dries faster than many analogues.

What to look for when buying

Look for Japanese versions on marketplaces or stationery stores. The name or description must indicate 0.38 mm (or 0.4 mm) - this will ensure that very thin and neat line that will not blur on the notepad paper.

item.title: USB via Qemu
item.content:encoded:
The easiest way to run multiboot USB via QEMU on Windows

  • Download QEMU for Windows regular installer.
  • Find out the flash drive number

PowerShell from administrator:

Get-CimInstance Win32_DiskDrive

Look for your USB flash drive.

For example: \.\PHYSICALDRIVE2

  1. Launch the flash drive

Open PowerShell as administrator:

cd "C:\Program Files\qemu"

.\qemu-system-x86_64.exe -m 4096 -boot c -hda \\.\PHYSICALDRIVE2

Folder for screenshots

🐧 Login TTY

[!NOTE] Mango > use Bash or ZSH or FISH

.bash_profile

if [[ -z $DISPLAY && $XDG_VTNR -eq 1 ]]; then
  exec mango
fi

.zprofile

if [ -z "${DISPLAY}" ] && [ "${XDG_VTNR}" -eq 1 ]; then
  exec mango
fi

config.fish

if status is-login
    if test (tty) = /dev/tty1

         set -gx XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP mango
            set -gx XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP mango
            set -gx XDG_SESSION_TYPE wayland
            set -gx MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND 1
            set -gx QT_QPA_PLATFORM wayland
            
            exec mango
    end
end

Login Mango

[!TIP] Arch Linux > login > pass

Mango + Sway

config.fish

[!TIP] Interactive session selection when logging into TTY1

if status is-interactive; and test (tty) = "/dev/tty1"
    echo "==================================="
    echo " Run Mango or Sway:   "
    echo " [1] Mango (Wayland)              "
    echo " [2] Sway (Wayland)              "
    echo " [3] Stay in TTY      "
    echo "==================================="
    
    # Read the user's choice
    read -P "Select [1-3]: " choice

    switch $choice
        case 1
            echo "Start Mango (Wayland)..."    
            set -gx XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP mango
            set -gx XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP mango
            set -gx XDG_SESSION_TYPE wayland
            set -gx MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND 1
            set -gx QT_QPA_PLATFORM wayland
            
            exec mango

        case 2
            echo "Start Sway (Wayland)..."
            set -gx XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP sway
            set -gx XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP sway
            set -gx XDG_SESSION_TYPE wayland
            set -gx MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND 1
            set -gx QT_QPA_PLATFORM wayland
            
            exec sway

        case 3
            echo "Enter to TTY!"
            
        case '*'
            echo "Bad step. Stay in TTY."
    end
end

Login Mango or Sway

├── [1] Mango (Wayland)   
├── [2] Sway (Wayland)   
└── [3] Stay in TTY

item.title: Multiboot USB
item.description: Support for Windows, Linux, WinPE, also for UEFI and MBR.
item.content:encoded:
import { Image } from 'astro:assets'; import image1 from './yellow.webp'; import image2 from './art.webp'; import image3 from './moda.webp'; import image4 from './city.webp';

[!TIP] Support for Windows, Linux, WinPE.
Support for UEFI and Legacy BIOS (MBR).

<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4"> <Image src={image1} alt="usb" /> <Image src={image2} alt="usb" /> <Image src={image3} alt="usb" /> <Image src={image4} alt="usb" /> </div>

Quick start

graph LR;
Format[Format] --> Boot[MBR/PBR]
Boot --> Files[USB-Files]
Files --> ISO[ISO]
ISO --> Menu[menu.lst]

Contents

  • Quick Start
  • Features
  • Supported Images
  • How to Make the USB Flash Drive Bootable
  • Preparing a Windows ISO Image
  • WinContig — Analysis and Defragmentation
  • Themes

Features

  • BIOS/UEFI
  • Windows ISO
  • Linux ISO
  • WinPE/LiveCD
  • Themes
  • Multiple ISOs on a single USB drive

Supported ISOs

  • Windows 10 / 11
  • Macrium Reflect
  • WinPE / LiveCD environments
  • Arch Linux
  • Kali Linux
  • CachyOS
  • Most modern Linux distributions

How to make the USB flash drive bootable

Installing the bootloader

[!IMPORTANT] The USB flash drive must be formatted as one partition.

Select a File System

FAT32/NTFS→ Choose the file system that best suits your needs.

[!IMPORTANT] FAT32 → does not support files larger than 4 GB

Activate the Partition

Open Bootice and select your USB drive.

Formatting a USB flash drive

File System
├─ FAT32/NTFS
└─ Start LBA → 2048
File system Features
FAT32 Compatible, but files up to 4 GB
NTFS Supports large ISO files 
Parts Manage
├─ Re-Partitioning
├─ USB-HDD mode (Single Partition)
└─ Activate

Install MBR

Bootice
└─ Process MBR
    └─Windows NT 5.x/6.x
        └─ Install

Install PBR

Bootice
└─ Process PBR
   └─ Grub4Dos
      └─ Install
         └─ Version 0.4.6a

Creating a Multiboot USB Drive

  • Format the USB flash drive using → Bootice → Parts Manage → Repartitioning.
  • Using BOOTICE, perform Re-Partitioning as described in the section above. → How ​​to make the USB flash drive bootable.
  • Copy the contents of the folder → USB-Files to the USB flash drive.
  • Integrate the driver → FiraDisk into the Windows ISO image.
  • Copy the ISO image to the folder → ISO.
  • Edit the file → menu.lst so that the ISO paths and names match.
  • Copy the Linux distributions to the TUX folder
  • Copy WinPE / LiveCD images to the PE folder

[!IMPORTANT] If desired, all ISOs can be stored in one directory.
Folders "ISO, TUX, PE, Apps" are created solely for convenience.

Structure of a multiboot flash drive

Multiboot USB root/
│
├──GFX/
│ ├── mac.gz
│ └── unifont.hex.gz
│
├── Apps/
│
├── ISO/
├── PE/
├── TUX/
│
├── AutoUnattend.xml
├── GRLDR
├── liveusbl
├── winpeshl.ini
│
└── menu.lst

[!IMPORTANT] A multiboot flash drive created using this scheme works in both BIOS Legacy and UEFI.

[!WARNING] Some ISO images may require disabling Secure Boot in the BIOS/UEFI to boot.

Preparing a Windows ISO image

To run Windows installation from a USB flash drive, you need to integrate the FiraDisk driver into the ISO image.
For this purpose → FiraDisk_integrator is used.

Create a working folder
├─ Use Latin characters in the folder name
├─ No spaces
├─ Maximum 8 characters
├─ Copy the Windows ISO into the folder
├─ Place the FiraDisk_integrator script in the same folder
└─ Run the script as administrator

[!IMPORTANT] You can copy several Windows ISO, of different editions and 32-bit and 64-bit versions.
The script processes all ISO images located in the same folder sequentially and, based on them, creates its own ISO images with the FiraDisk driver.

WinContig — Analysis & Defragmentation

When working with multiboot flash drives, ISO files should not be fragmented.

[!IMPORTANT] If the ISO is fragmented, errors or problems may occur while loading the ISO into memory.

ISO check

WinContig → Analyze

[!IMPORTANT] If the program shows the need for optimization, perform defragmentation.

Defragmentation→ launch WinContig

List of drives
├─ Select flash drive
├─ Properties
├─ Service
├─ Check
└─ Optimize

Themes

Themes → located in the make_skins/skins folder

How to Install a New Theme

Select the skin file → for example → mac.gz   
├─ Copy it to the folder → GFX
├─ Edit → menu.lst 
├─ Find the line → gfxmenu /GFX/sony.gz
└─ Replace → sony.gz with mac.gz

GitHub

Source files, configs, and themes:

  • Multiboot USB
  • Multiboot USB на русском

item.description: Notepad4 themes for Windows. Notepad4 is a light-weight text editor with syntax highlighting, code folding, auto-completion and rewritten in modern C++.
item.content:encoded:
Notepad4 - is a light-weight text editor for Windows with syntax highlighting, code folding, auto-completion and rewritten in modern C++.

[!TIP] Swenska Light - light theme.
Swenska Dark - dark theme.

For use Swenska Light in Notepad4:

  • install fonts from fonts folder.
  • run Notepad4.exe
  • select in menu - Scheme - Style Theme - Default.
  • select in menu - Scheme - customize Schemes.
  • import Swenska Light.ini from "themes" folder.

For use Swenska Dark in Notepad4:

  • install fonts from fonts folder.
  • run Notepad4.exe
  • select in menu - Scheme - Style Theme - Dark.
  • select in menu - Scheme - customize Schemes.
  • import Swenska Dark.ini from "themes" folder.

[!TIP] Or just download folder Notepad4 with pre-installed themes and use it.

Swenska Notepad4 download from the GitHub.
